statement_record.book: A subobject of X is a mono m : M >-> X; a morphism of subobjects m -> m' is an arrow f of the slice C/X (m' ∘ f = m); these form a category Sub_C(X), which is a preorder because m' is monic so at most one such f exists. Inclusion m ⊆ m' means such an f exists; m ≡ m' means mutual inclusion, i.e. isomorphism in Sub_C(X).

evidence.intree_statement: A subobject of an object x is (an equivalence class of) a monomorphism into x. Here the setoid structure itself carries the quotient: two monos into x are equivalent when there is an isomorphism of their domains commuting with them over x.
#[export] Program Instance SubObj_Setoid : Setoid (SubObj x) := { equiv := fun u v => { i : sub_dom u ≅ sub_dom v & sub_mono v ∘ to i ≈ sub_mono u } }.
Theorem classifier_classifies (x : C) : @Isomorphism Sets {| carrier := SubObj x |} {| carrier := x ~> Ω |}.

Theorem sets_char_subobject@{o so} {A B : SetoidObject@{o o}} (m : A ~{Sets@{o so}}~> B) (Hm : @Monic Sets@{o so} A B m) : @equiv _ (@SubObj_Setoid Sets@{o so} B) (@Build_SubObj Sets@{o so} B A m Hm) (@Build_SubObj Sets@{o so} B (Sets_Image m) (Sets_Image_mono m) (Sets_Image_mono_monic m)).
Definition Pow {C : Category} {H : ElementaryTopos C} (a : C) : C := Ω ^ a.
Example FinSet_Pow_two : @Pow FinSet FinSet_Topos 2%nat = 4%nat := eq_refl.

statement_record.book: It is convenient to replace the preorder Sub_C(X) by the poset obtained by quotienting by ≡ (mutual inclusion); under that reading a subobject IS an equivalence class of monos into X. In Sets this poset is isomorphic to the powerset: Sub_Sets(X) = P(X), every subobject being represented by a unique subset.
statement_record.intree: The quotient reading is the library's DEFAULT: `SubObj_Setoid` makes the setoid equivalence on `SubObj x` be exactly mutual factorization (via `sub_equiv_iff_mutual`), and the header states 'the setoid structure itself carries the quotient'. The Sets-side statement appears as `sets_char_subobject`: every mono `m : A ~> B` of Sets is `SubObj_Setoid`-equal to the sub-setoid `Sets_Image m ⊆ B`. The general classification is `classifier_classifies : SubObj x ≅ (x ~> Ω)` in Sets.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: the quotient half is present (indeed built in), and the 'unique subset representative' half is proved for Sets as `sets_char_subobject`. What is missing is the POSET structure on the quotient and the isomorphism with a powerset OBJECT: `Sub_Sets(X) ≅ P(X)` cannot be stated in-tree for the library's `Sets`, which has no `SubobjectClassifier` instance (only cross-universe theorems, by the documented size obstruction) and no powerset object for setoids.

Record IsPullback {C : Category} {x y z : C} (f : x ~> z) (g : y ~> z) (P : C) (p1 : P ~> x) (p2 : P ~> y) := { is_pullback_commutes : f ∘ p1 ≈ g ∘ p2; is_pullback_ump : ∀ Q (q1 : Q ~> x) (q2 : Q ~> y), f ∘ q1 ≈ g ∘ q2 → ∃! u : Q ~> P, p1 ∘ u ≈ q1 ∧ p2 ∘ u ≈ q2 }.
Class HasPullbacks (C : Category) : Type := { pullback : forall {x y z : C} (f : x ~> z) (g : y ~> z), Pullback f g }.
Definition Pullback_Limit {C : Category} (F : Cospan C) := Limit F.

statement_record.book: A pullback of f : A -> C and g : B -> C is an object P with p1 : P -> A, p2 : P -> B such that f p1 = g p2, universal: for every Z, z1 : Z -> A, z2 : Z -> B with f z1 = g z2 there is a UNIQUE u : Z -> P with z1 = p1 u and z2 = p2 u. The object is written A ×_C B, the mediator ⟨z1,z2⟩.

Definition finset_pb_pred {m n k : nat} (f : Fin.t m → Fin.t k) (g : Fin.t n → Fin.t k) : Fin.t (m * n) → bool := fun p => fin_eqb (f (fst (fin_unpair p))) (g (snd (fin_unpair p))).

evidence.intree_statement: Definition sub_reindex {x y : C} (f : y ~> x) (u : SubObj x) : SubObj y := {| sub_dom := Pull f (sub_mono u) (pullback f (sub_mono u)); sub_mono := pullback_fst f (sub_mono u) (pullback f (sub_mono u)); sub_is_monic := monic_pullback_stable f (sub_mono u) (sub_is_monic u) (pullback f (sub_mono u)) |}.
Lemma monic_pullback_stable {C : Category} {x y z : C} (f : x ~> z) (m : y ~> z) (Hm : Monic m) (P : Pullback f m) : Monic (pullback_fst f m P).
#[export] Instance sub_reindex_respects {x y : C} (f : y ~> x) : Proper (equiv ==> equiv) (@sub_reindex x y f).
Lemma sub_reindex_id {x : C} (u : SubObj x) : sub_reindex id u ≈ u.
Lemma sub_reindex_comp {x y z : C} (g : y ~> x) (f : z ~> y) (u : SubObj x) : sub_reindex (g ∘ f) u ≈ sub_reindex f (sub_reindex g u).

Program Definition Sub : C^op ⟶ Sets := {| fobj := fun x : C => {| carrier := SubObj x ; is_setoid := @SubObj_Setoid C x |}; fmap := fun x y (f : x ~{C^op}~> y) => {| morphism := sub_reindex (unop f) ; proper_morphism := sub_reindex_respects (unop f) |} |}.

statement_record.book: In any category, given f : A -> B and a subobject m : M >-> B, form the pullback A ×_B M of m along f with leg m' : A ×_B M -> A. Since m is monic so is m' (left as an exercise), so pulling back along f defines a map f^{-1} : Sub(B) -> Sub(A), m ↦ m'. Section 5.3 will show f^{-1} is a functor, hence M ≡ N implies f^{-1}(M) ≡ f^{-1}(N).
statement_record.intree: `sub_reindex f u : SubObj y` is exactly m ↦ (pullback of `sub_mono u` along f, first projection), with monicity supplied by `monic_pullback_stable`. `sub_reindex_respects : Proper (equiv ==> equiv) (sub_reindex f)` is the ≡-invariance the book promises, and `sub_reindex_id`/`sub_reindex_comp` (the latter via `pullback_paste`) assemble `Sub : C^op ⟶ Sets`.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-stronger: the exercise the book defers (pullback of a mono is a mono) is proved as `monic_pullback_stable`; the functoriality announced for §5.3 is already discharged here (`sub_reindex_id`, `sub_reindex_comp`, `sub_reindex_respects`, packaged as the presheaf `Sub`), and there is an extra invariance in the MORPHISM argument (`sub_reindex_respects_mor : f ≈ f' → sub_reindex f u ≈ sub_reindex f' u`) which the book does not mention. Requires `HasPullbacks C` (chosen pullbacks) where the book merely forms 'the' pullback; the chosen-vs-any discrepancy is bridged by `sub_reindex_transport`.
